name: atomic-json-write-via-temp-rename
description: Plot's writeJsonAtomic in src/io.ts serializes to a sibling ${path}.tmp.<8 hex> file, then rename(2)s into place under withFileLock. Mirrors mulch's writeExpertiseFile pattern (port of utils/lock.ts and utils/expertise.ts). The lock is per-target-path; tmp filename is random so concurrent same-path writers don't collide on tmp.

content: Plot JSON files are serialized with stableStringify (src/io.ts): deep-sorted object keys + 2-space indent + trailing newline. This is the load-bearing convention behind SPEC §4.2's 'clean semantic diffs in git'. Arrays preserve their natural order — sorting arrays is the caller's responsibility.

name: jsonl-append-under-file-lock
description: appendEvent in src/io.ts wraps fs/promises.appendFile in withFileLock on the events file itself (not a sibling). This serializes intra-process concurrent appenders so JSONL lines don't interleave; readEvents can run lockless because partial-line risk only exists during a write and the lock prevents that.

content: withFileLock(path) acquires an O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock at ${path}.lock; re-acquiring the same path from inside the callback deadlocks until timeout. For callers that need to hold the lock across multiple writes, use writeJsonAtomicWithinLock and appendEventWithinLock from src/io.ts — they skip the lock and assume the caller already holds it.
